Subject: Streaming model fit and UX for Acme Health - next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier - that was helpful. A quick recap from our side and what we'd like to confirm before we run an eval: 

- Goal: real-time clinical note summarization for telehealth sessions. Primary constraints are partial-output coherence (users get partial sentences), stop sequences (we need clean termination), and 200-300ms token latency target for streaming.
- Concern: previous POC with another provider showed repeated partial sentences when streaming long contexts. We want to avoid degraded UX.
- What we need from Redwood: recommended model(s) for quality/latency tradeoffs, a small benchmark run (50 sessions) using our sample prompts, and guidance on stop sequences/partial output heuristics.

Next steps from Acme: share a redacted sample of 50 sessions and agree on evaluation metrics. Can Redwood propose a plan & timeline?

Thanks,
Alex

Acme Health

Alex - great to hear the call was useful. Appreciate the clear constraints. Quick reply with a proposed plan and the initial recommendations: 

Proposed "mini-eval" plan:
- Redwood will run a 50-session streaming eval against the sample redacted sessions you provide.
- Metrics: token-level latency distribution (p50/p90/p99), partial-output coherence score (syntactic completeness), stop-sequence failure rate, overall ROUGE/BLEU for summarization where applicable.
- Timeline: we can kick off once we get samples; expected turnaround 5 business days for the initial report.

Recommended starting models:
- rwd-3b-stream (recommended): good balance of throughput and coherence in our streaming benchmarks.
- rwd-7b-quant (alt): higher quality but may need tuned batching and quantization; expect higher latency unless pinned to Dedicated.

Quick tips for streaming UX we'll apply in the eval:
- Soft-stop heuristics: implement both explicit stop sequences and an end-of-turn confidence threshold to avoid mid-sentence cuts.
- Partial output buffering: hold small token windows (e.g., 50-80ms) before emitting to improve sentence-level coherence while keeping latency low.
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm KV cache for known session prefixes to reduce first-token latency.

Attachments included: acme_streaming_benchmark_v1.csv (sample benchmark template), prompt_set_v1.md (recommended prompt set + stop sequences).

Can you confirm delivery of the 50 redacted sessions and whether we should use the exact stop tokens you currently have or propose new ones? Once confirmed, Jordan will scope an eval run and Connor will advise on streaming config if you want to target p90 latency < 300ms.

- Marissa

Alex/Marissa - looping Connor in for the deep-dive. Brief technical response and a proposed mutual action plan below.

Notes on partial-output coherence / tail-regressions:
- Background audio and overlapping speech can produce low-confidence model tokens; strategies we recommend:
  1) Confidence thresholding: tag tokens with a streaming confidence score and suppress emissions below a tuned threshold (then re-emit corrected text after the next stable punctuation).
  2) Micro-buffering: as Marissa suggested, hold tokens for ~60ms by default; for highly punctuated outputs increase to 100ms. This reduces mid-sentence chops with minimal UX impact.
  3) Post-stream stitching: run a quick light-weight non-streamed pass on the final 1-2 seconds of the buffer to patch partial sentences before final commit.

Stop sequence handling:
- Using a unique hard token like "--END--" is fine; in streaming we recommend emitting a soft signal on detection and confirming with either a short confidence window or explicit silence detection from your transcripts to avoid premature cutoff.

Latency & model selection:
- rwd-3b-stream pinned on Redwood Hosted with continuous batching tuned to small windows should meet p90 < 300ms in our tests for similar workloads. We will run the benchmark to validate with your samples.
- If p90 > 300ms on Hosted, we recommend Redwood Dedicated with pinned capacity and reduced batching (or running rwd-3b on higher-clock GPUs).

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Acme: deliver 50 redacted sessions + existing stop-token list (action: Alex) - due 2026-06-15
- Redwood (Marissa/Jordan): run 50-session streaming eval, include metrics and suggested config changes - deliverable 5 business days after samples received
- Redwood (Connor): provide a short runbook for stop-sequence soft-confirmation + micro-buffering knobs to tune in your client SDK
- Follow-up: schedule a 30-min results review + decision on Hosted vs Dedicated

Attachment: streaming_eval_plan.pdf (proposed eval steps and acceptance criteria).

I'll start the eval template as soon as we get the data. Marissa - happy to coordinate procurement/PO items if we need to move to Dedicated.
